newsitem.title: POLAND: PepsiCo restaurant unit eyes E.Europe growth.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo restaurant unit eyes E.Europe growth.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc. said Monday it plans to increase its number of restaurants in Poland to 170 from 49 in the next three to five years under a spun-off company that includes its KFC, Pizza Hut and Taco Bell businesses.

Peter Maslen, president of PepsiCo's restaurant division for Central Europe, told a news briefing that PepsiCo's late-January decision to spin off its restaurant business should help units of the new company gain investment capital.

"It (PepsiCo's separation) gives us faster access to capital and resources ... rather than having to stand beside my beverage colleagues ... I really only have to compete with the other restaurant companies," Maslen said.
He said his company had already invested $57 million in Poland since 1993, with employment, currently at 3,000, likely to rise to 10,000 in three to five years.

Maslen said Poland was the region's most promising market not only because of its population of 40 million, rapid economic growth and literate work force, but also because of the entrepeneurial nature of the people.
John Wells, CEO of Wedel, majority-owned by Pepsico, said that despite rumours, he had no knowledge of a plan by the parent company to increase or decrease its share in the Polish confectioner.
PepsiCo's stock fell 25 cents to $34.625 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
